correctness.rationale: New-entry event requires one uniquely missing coupon in the common (M−1)-block and matching entering coupon; independence and inclusion-exclusion derive weighted flux. Finite occupancy-number derivatives yield exact κ_{n,M}; leading positive (n−1)/n² (M−1)(M−2)((n−1)/n)^(M−3) for fixed n ensures local minimum, not global all-n optimizer. For n=2, derivative of μ=(t+t^M)/(1+t)^(M+1) has sign 1−Mt+Mt^(M−1)−t^M; monotonic derivative structure yields unique inner root for all M≥4 and only two globally maximizing asymmetric probabilities; M=2,3 have only balanced maximum. Independently checked polynomial Hessian coefficient for several n,M. Claimed asymptotic rare-one-type example is correct but known contextual bound.

value.rationale: A natural optimization problem exhibits an exact, nontrivial binary bifurcation at M=4, and an explicit all-alphabet finite-window local stability test for the same stochastic entrance functional. Unlike the known global asymptotic optimizer, these give finite-window structure and a sharp symmetry-breaking boundary, an independently useful mathematical classification.

final_claim: Exact finite-M tangent Hessian of stationary expiring-coupon entrance flux for n types, eventual strict local minimum at uniform for every fixed n, and sharp n=2 global optimizer switch M=2,3 balanced versus exactly two asymmetric maxima for every M≥4.
limitations: Claim does not characterize all global optimizers for n≥3 or the initial completion-time distribution.
